claims.text: The high-temperature plastic strain and toughness of as-cast equimolar WTaTiVZr are governed by its solidification-induced dendritic microstructure.
The alloy segregates into W-Ta-rich dendrites and Zr-Ti-rich interdendritic regions.
Vanadium is distributed throughout both the dendritic and interdendritic regions.
The W-Ta-rich dendrites and Zr-Ti-rich interdendritic regions are both BCC phases.
W-Ta-rich dendrites provide multicomponent solid-solution strengthening.
Lattice distortion in the W-Ta-rich dendrites contributes to the alloy's high strength.
Zr-Ti-rich interdendritic regions modify dislocation cores.
Zr-Ti-rich interdendritic regions improve grain-boundary cohesion.
Zr-Ti-rich interdendritic regions promote localized plastic flow that impedes crack propagation.
Arc melting elemental powders of greater than 99.99% purity with at least five remelts produces a dendritic WTaTiVZr microstructure.
Relative to powder-sintered pure tungsten, WTaTiVZr is expected to have higher yield and ultimate strength at room and elevated temperatures.
Relative to powder-sintered pure tungsten, WTaTiVZr is expected to exhibit greater plastic strain and a lower brittle-to-ductile transition temperature.
Relative to powder-sintered pure tungsten, WTaTiVZr is expected to exhibit less scratch-induced cracking and greater scratch-based fracture toughness.
The pure-tungsten baseline has a single-phase BCC structure with coarse equiaxed grains of approximately 100 ± 20 µm.
The pure-tungsten baseline has an indentation-derived yield strength of approximately 700 MPa at room temperature and 250 MPa at 500 °C.
The pure-tungsten baseline exhibits negligible plasticity up to 300 °C.
The pure-tungsten baseline has a scratch-based fracture toughness of approximately 25 ± 1 MPa√m.
As-cast WTaTiVZr may remain relatively brittle between 25 and 200 °C.
